title: Photography: aperture, shutter and ISO
examples: What is the exposure triangle in photography?
How does aperture affect my photo?
Can you explain the difference between shutter speed and aperture?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the exposure triangle in photography. This triangle helps us control how bright our pictures are.
Aperture is the opening inside your camera lens. A wider aperture lets in more light for your picture.
Shutter speed controls how long the camera takes the picture. A slower speed captures more light, but can cause blur.

draw.text: Shutter Speed: Time light hits sensor

explain.say: ISO measures how sensitive your camera's sensor is to light. A higher ISO helps in dark places, but adds digital noise.
To get a bright picture, you need to balance these three elements. Changing one usually means changing another.
Think about photographing a fast-moving dog in the park. You need a fast shutter speed to freeze its action.

faq.a: It is a concept showing how aperture, shutter speed, and ISO work together. They must be balanced to get the right brightness.
asks: How do these three things relate?
Do I have to change all three settings?

faq.q: If I use a wide aperture, what happens to my picture?
faq.a: A wide aperture lets in a lot of light, which makes your picture brighter. It also helps blur the background.
asks: Does aperture control depth of field?
What is the effect of a large aperture setting?

faq.q: Why do I need to worry about shutter speed?
faq.a: Shutter speed controls how long the light hits the sensor. A slow speed captures motion blur, which is useful for water.
asks: How do I use shutter speed for action shots?

faq.q: What is the best ISO to use?
faq.a: There is no single best ISO. You choose it based on the light available. Lower ISO is best in bright daylight.
asks: Does high ISO always mean bad photos?
When should I increase my ISO setting?

faq.q: Can I change just one setting and keep the photo bright?
faq.a: You can, but it is hard. Changing one setting will usually require you to change another to keep the brightness correct.
asks: Is it possible to fix exposure with just one dial?
What if I only change the aperture?

facts: Aperture controls the amount of light passing through the lens.
Slower shutter speeds can create motion blur effects.
Higher ISO increases the sensor's sensitivity to light.
The three elements work together to achieve correct exposure.

quiz.say: To freeze the movement of a bird flying quickly, which setting should you use?
quiz.show: Freezing fast action needs a fast shutter speed.
quiz.why: A fast shutter speed means the camera takes a picture very quickly, stopping any movement.

wrong.0: Aperture controls light amount, not how fast the action is.
wrong.1: ISO controls sensitivity, which affects noise, not speed.
wrong.2: This would blur the bird instead of freezing it.

quiz.say: If you are in a very dark room, which setting should you increase?
quiz.show: Dark room needs more light: Increase ISO.
quiz.why: Increasing the ISO makes the sensor more sensitive, helping capture enough light in the dark.

wrong.0: While a tripod helps, you still need to adjust ISO or aperture.
wrong.2: A narrow aperture lets in less light, making it darker.
wrong.3: A fast shutter speed lets in light for too short a time.

quiz.say: If you use a very wide aperture, what is a common visual effect?
quiz.why: Wide apertures blur the background, making the subject stand out more.

wrong.0: While it adds light, the specific effect is background blur.
wrong.2: This relates to slow shutter speed, not aperture size.
wrong.3: Noise is usually related to high ISO, not aperture.
